To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the toxicity of carbamates and some organophosphate inhibitors of acetylcho- linesterase can be greatly reduced, in the guinea-pig and the rabbit, by pretreatment with certain other organophosphate compounds, followed by the oxime P2S and the anticholinergic drug trihexyphenidyl.

the toxicity of carbamate, organophosphorus, and nerve agents can be greatly reduced in guinea pigs and rabbits by prior administration of an organophosphorus compound, such as ethyl-4nitrophenyl methyl-phosphonate, followed by oximes, such as P2S and atropine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method for the protection of animals against organophosphorus poisoning.
the development of methods for the treatment of poisoning with organophosphorus nerve poisons.
a new approach to the treatment of poisoning by organophosphorus insecticides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the guinea-pig and rabbit, a combination of an organophosphorus compound, an oxime, and atropine can be used to protect animals against the toxicity of Soman, but that the most effective organophosphorus protective compound has not been found.

a combination of pretreatment with ethyl-4- nitrophenyl methyl phosphonate followed by oxime (P2S) and cholinolytic (anticholinergic) drug, such as atropine or hyoscyamine, can provide a very high degree of protection against Soman (1,2,2 -trimethylpropyl methyl phosphono-fluoridoate) in guinea pigs.

the toxicity of carbamate or organophosphorus insecticides can be greatly reduced, but not eliminated, by the administration, prior to the insecticides, of an effective organophosphorus anticholinesterase compound, followed by an oxime and atropeine or other anticholinergic compound.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the guinea pig is more susceptible to Soman than the rat, but is more easily protected against Soman by pretreatment with organophosphorus compound followed by oxime.
the guinea pig is the species most likely to respond to the form of treatment described.

, in the guinea-pig, the toxicity of carbamates and organophosphorus esters can be reduced by prior administration, followed by oximes and atrophine, of some other organphosphorus compounds which are themselves reduced in toxicity by oximes and cholinolytics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the toxicity of carbamate or organophosphorus (OP) compounds can be greatly mitigated by pretreatment with an organophosphorus compound, oxime, and cholinolytic drug.
the toxicity of a number of organophosphorus and carbamate compounds, which are not reduced by oxime, can be reduced by pretreatment with an organophosphorus compound followed by oxime treatment.

the use of oximes and anticholinesterases to mitigate the effects of organophosphates poisoning is limited to certain circumstances and that the use of these agents in the treatment of poisoning with carbamates or other organophosphates that do not react with oximes and antimuscarinics should be avoided.
